List the grids of a Dataset

Source: R/grids.R
xr_grids.Rd

A grid is the set of variables that share one set of dimensions, as tidync's grids are: ERA5's 273 variables are two grids, a surface grid over (time, latitude, longitude) and a pressure-level grid over (time, level, latitude, longitude). Each grid can be read as one table, with a column per member: give tbl() its name, or several of its variables. xarray has no grid object; this listing groups the variables by their dimensions. Only metadata is read.

Usage

xr_grids(con, view = c("meaning", "storage"))

Arguments

con

an XarrayConnection

view

"meaning" or "storage", see Details

Value

a tibble, one row per grid, most dimensions first, then most variables: grid, its dimensions joined by commas (the name tbl() takes); ndims; cells, the product of the dimension sizes (NA in the storage view for a grid whose arrays store a character dimension); n, the number of variables; the list column variables; and chunkings, the number of distinct storage chunk shapes among them (a grid whose members share a key space has 1). The meaning view adds the list column coords, the coordinates whose dimensions lie within the grid; the storage view adds roles, how many of the arrays are data variables, coordinates and dimension coordinates.

Details

Two views:

  • "meaning" (the default) groups data variables by their dimensions as xarray decodes them, taken as a set ((lat, lon) and (lon, lat) are one grid), and lists the coordinates that belong to each grid. These are the grids a table can be built over.

  • "storage" groups every stored array, coordinates included, by its dimensions as stored, in order. A character array that xarray decodes to strings keeps its character dimension (encoding["char_dim_name"]), so a netCDF file lists the grids tidync (through ncmeta) finds: 16 in an Argo profile file where the meaning view has 5.

See also

tbl() to read a grid as a table; xr_chunks() for its chunk map; xrdbi-package for an overview.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## needs a Python environment with xarray (see ?xrdbi)
f <- system.file("extdata/autotest/two_vars_scale_offset.nc",
                 package = "xrdbi")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), f)
xr_grids(con)
xr_grids(con, "storage")
dbDisconnect(con)
} # }
